failure.case: male: landing carries movement without the standing tail and preserves old exports
failure.assertion: After an airborne Run input, canvas action is still jump and pending action is run

diagnosis: The test waited for any Jump position >=9, then awaited separate observer setup, a Playwright click and a transient-attribute assertion. The source clock continues through those round trips, allowing landing before the assertion. Matching SHA passes the entire PR suite. This is evidence of a test scheduling race, not an export/frame/route failure; the log alone does not establish a device-level performance cause.
fix: Arm an in-page MutationObserver before takeoff. At the first painted airborne pose >=9 and before the reviewed landing, click the existing Run/Idle control once in that browser task. Capture input action/position/time, then assert the recorded Jump+pending target state and original landing-frame/phase assertions after completion. No native clock mocking, increased waits or relaxed expected frames.
validation: Both modified landing-run browser cases passed locally (5.7m), including actual airborne Run/Idle pending samples, both views, current/historical imports and exact export comparison. See landing-e2e.log.gz and export-equivalence.json.
